source.title: Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design
source.authors: Bojian Hou; Xiao-Long Liu; Xiao-Yi Liu; Jia-Qi Xu; Yasmine Badr; Meng-Yue Hang; Sudhanshu Chanpuriya; Jun Zhou; Yu-Hang Yang; Han Xu; Qiu-Ling Suo; La-Ming Chen; Yuxi Hu; Jia-Sheng Zhang; Huaqing Xiong; Yu-Zhen Huang; Chaochao Chen; Yue Dong; Yi Yang; Shuo Chang; Xiao-Rui Gan; Wen-Lin Chen; Santanu Kolay; Darren Liu; Jade Nie; Chun-Che Yang; Ellie Wen; Ji-Yan Yang; Hua-Yu Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports scaling results for recommendation systems, a different application setting from language-model pretraining, using normalized entropy and recommendation-model compute/depth sweeps.
record.gate_note: The study's own experiments vary recommendation-model compute and layer count and report normalized-entropy (NE) results. It does not test language-model pretraining loss. Cited language-model scaling results and the paper's component-efficiency ablations are not counted as scaling-law rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports normalized entropy (NE, a normalized cross-entropy loss) against per-sample compute and layer count for CTR recommendation models. That is a new setting with its own result bearing on V5. It does not test language-model pretraining.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Kunlun gives predictable scaling (NE linear in log compute) for joint sequence and non-sequence recommendation, with about 2× InterFormer's scaling slope and higher MFU (17%→37%). The '2×' refers to the slope; at 180 GFLOPs the NE-gain advantage is 1.58×.
record.recipe_differences: This is a recommendation-system scaling study, not language-model pretraining. It uses NE and recommendation-model compute/depth comparisons rather than held-out language-model loss sweeps over parameters, tokens, and training compute.

fits_no_version.finding: The slope of NE versus log(compute) differs by architecture: Kunlun's is about 2× InterFormer's, and gains over Wukong grow with scale for Kunlun (0.31% to 0.79%). The authors attribute this to hardware utilization (MFU) and allocation efficiency.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In recommendation models, the scaling coefficient depends strongly on architecture and hardware efficiency, not only on compute.

record.problems: The experiments use internal Meta Ads datasets, and the text does not report uncertainty estimates or state that the NE measurements are on a held-out split. The compute comparison has three scales; the paper also says NE values are not comparable across scales because feature configurations differ. Its scaling and extrapolation claims are therefore limited to the tested recommendation setting.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 component ablations and the production deployment result are omitted because they do not report a scaling-law result. Wukong's Table 3 entries are marked only as the baseline and do not give separate numeric NE gains.

untested.parts: Image/video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are untested. Only CTR recommendation models over roughly 1.5 orders of magnitude of per-sample forward FLOPs were tested; training tokens and total training compute were not varied.
The authors assert that the curves enable extrapolation but report no held-out prediction of a larger run.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.

missing.what: NE improvement versus total GFLOPs curves. Kunlun: +0.30%, +0.45%, +0.61%, +0.80%. Baseline/InterFormer: +0.16%, +0.25%, +0.33%, +0.44%. Both span about 50–200 GFLOPs. These are the main loss-versus-compute evidence.
Layer-sweep numeric values: NE gain and GFLOPs per layer count (1L–6L: 0–0.37%, 45–169 GFLOPs).
Claim that adding Wukong experts (width) gives power-law gains, with no numbers reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's rows r1–r9 are architecture-versus-baseline gains within each scale. By the authors' own note, these cannot show the loss-compute form, so they are relinked to none. The functional form used, NE = NE0 − η·log(C/C0), is logarithmic; the authors call it a power law in the log domain, but it is not the L ∝ C^−α form of the originals. Compute is per-sample forward FLOPs, not training compute. The data are internal and there are no error bars.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model pretraining loss sweep in parameters, tokens, or compute; the experiments concern recommendation systems and NE.
No reported prediction of much larger runs from fits to smaller runs.
No fixed-compute sweep finding loss-minimizing parameter and token allocations.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Tests compute and depth scaling in CTR recommendation systems only. Does not test image/video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or language-model pretraining.
Reports CTR prediction quality in recommendation models, not downstream language-model task performance as a function of pretraining loss or scale.
Does not compare fitting choices or establish that published language-model exponents or compute-optimal allocations depend on setup.

rows.subject: Kunlun (Ours)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of layers from 1 to 6 and measured NE improvement.
rows.measure: NE improvement as a function of layer count
rows.value: The text reports consistent gains with diminishing returns and gives ∆NE_l ≈ c / log(l + 1).
rows.note: The specific layer-by-layer values are not stated in the text; the figure presents the trend.
rows.check: This is the only row measuring loss versus scale within one model. The value can be read from Figure 4 (right): NE gain 0%, 0.10%, 0.16%, 0.24%, 0.31%, 0.37% for 1–6 layers, at about 45–169 GFLOPs. The stated form c/log(l+1) is asserted, not shown with fit statistics. The baseline is the 1-layer model, not 'not stated'.

relationships.condition: CTR recommendation models (Kunlun, InterFormer) on Meta Ads data, about 45–200 per-sample GFLOPs, single epoch
relationships.reason: NE improves monotonically with compute and depth, with diminishing returns (r10; Figure 4 left values missing from rows). However, the fitted form is linear in log C, not a power law. The range is under two orders of magnitude, with no fit quality or uncertainty, and the authors say cross-scale NEs use different feature configs.
relationships.display_finding: NE improved monotonically with compute and depth but showed diminishing returns under a fit linear in log compute, across less than two orders of magnitude and differing feature configurations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Kunlun and comparator recommendation systems in the reported compute sweeps, plus Kunlun's 1-to-6-layer sweep
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports recommendation-model NE gains across three compute scales and diminishing, predictable gains with layer count; see r1–r10. This supports scaling behavior in this recommendation setting, not the other modalities or regimes listed in V5.
